payload.title: [crypto-e2ee-5] Monotonic #highestSeen can be permanently poisoned by a single forged high-epochId announcement,...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING crypto-e2ee-5 (medium/dos, confidence=medium, verify-votes +1/-1)

FILE: packages/core/src/e2ee.ts
LINES: 1118-1135, 1486-1505, 359-363

WHAT: poll() ignores any announcement with epochId <= #highestSeen (lines 1122, 1492) and there is no upper bound or sanity check on the adopted epochId (header epochId is a uint32; adopt() accepts any number > current). Combined with the lack of sender authentication (crypto-e2ee-4), a single forged `keyEpoch` signal carrying a very large epochId (e.g. 2^31) sets #highestSeen to that value (and, if unwrappable, adopt() sets current to it). Legitimate subsequent announcements — whose epochIds advance by 1 from 0 — are all <= #highestSeen and silently dropped forever.

IMPACT: One forged announcement permanently breaks key-epoch adoption for a victim: it never converges on real epochs again, so it cannot decrypt any future media — a durable denial of service requiring only the ability to place one signal on the relay.

SUGGESTED FIX: Reject epochIds that jump implausibly far beyond the current epoch, gate adoption on an authenticated sender (crypto-e2ee-4), and/or bound epochId growth relative to observed membership churn.
